name: Mount Everest
scope: The highest point on Earth's surface, on the Nepal-Tibet border (8,848.86 m by the 2020 China-Nepal joint survey). A KEYSTONE deep ladder, one distinct wonder per rung. T1: the grey limestone at the very SUMMIT is full of the fossils of sea creatures -- the top of the world was once the warm, shallow floor of an ancient SEA (Ordovician marine limestone, ~450 Mya; trilobites/crinoids). T1: Tibetans call it Chomolungma -- answer the meaning, 'Goddess Mother of the World' (Nepali Sagarmatha = 'brow/head of the sky'). T2: above ~8,000 m the air holds too little oxygen to keep a body alive for long -- climbers call this the 'death zone.' T2: Everest is one of exactly fourteen peaks on Earth over 8,000 m -- the 'eight-thousanders.' T3: just below the summit climbers had to conquer a near-vertical rock band, now named for the man who first climbed it in 1953 -- the Hillary Step. T3: the deadliest stretch of the standard route is a shifting, collapsing river of ice at the mountain's foot -- the Khumbu Icefall. T3: the summit is so high the jet stream blasts it at 200+ mph, so climbers wait for a brief calm 'weather window' in May. T4: Everest is the highest mountain ABOVE SEA LEVEL, but measured base-to-summit it is beaten -- Hawaii's Mauna Kea is taller from its ocean-floor base. T5: Everest is STILL GROWING ~2 mm a year, and a 2024 study found a nearby river (the Arun/Kosi) eroded away so much rock that the crust 'floats' upward -- isostatic rebound -- adding extra height. T5: modern wonder/caution -- the crowded summit ridge and single-file 'traffic jams' in the death zone.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Everest; montana.edu/everest (Summit Limestone, Naming); iugs-geoheritage.org (Ordovician rocks of Everest); UCL News + Sci.News + Nature Geoscience 2024 (Kosi/Arun river uplift, ~2mm/yr, isostatic rebound); Britannica 'Mount Everest'. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first per pipeline.
framing_note: Voice: scene-led wonder, never 'What is the tallest mountain?'. The T1 marine-fossil rung (seashells on the roof of the world) is the opener; the STILL-RISING / river-capture isostatic-rebound rung is the T5 payoff, and the Mauna Kea 'highest vs tallest' rung is the dinner-test twist. Accuracy rail: height is 8,848.86 m (2020 joint survey), summit rock is Ordovician marine limestone, uplift is ~2 mm/yr (NOT 4). Every answer stays a place-fact; distractors = other real 8,000ers (K2, Kangchenjunga, Lhotse) and real summit features (South Col, Western Cwm). Lane border: Himalayan wildlife (yak, snow leopard) is the ANIMAL bank -- keep answers on the mountain and its rock.
history_overlap: The 1953 Hillary & Tenzing first ascent may be a history-bank episode; here it is deliberately reframed as the PLACE-feature (the Hillary Step), not the expedition narrative -- keep the answer the named rock band, not the bare human names.

name: The Himalayas
scope: The world's highest mountain SYSTEM, arcing ~2,400 km along the India-Eurasia collision. Deep ladder on the range as a whole (single peaks get their own ladders). T1: behind the peaks lies a plateau so high and vast it is nicknamed the 'Roof of the World' -- the Tibetan Plateau. T2: the range holds ALL fourteen of Earth's peaks over 8,000 m -- nowhere else on the planet has mountains this high. T2: the Himalayas are STILL RISING because two continents are colliding -- India is crashing into Asia. T3: India was once a separate ISLAND continent that drifted north and slammed into Asia ~50 million years ago; it is still plowing in a few cm a year. T3: the peaks are built of MARINE rock -- the collision closed an ocean (the Tethys), so seabed limestone now sits miles up. T4: the wall of mountains wrings the summer monsoon dry, leaving a bone-dry 'rain shadow' desert on the Tibetan side (teach: rain shadow). T4: the range is the water tower of Asia -- the Ganges, Indus, and Brahmaputra all rise from its snows. T5: the collision doesn't just push up -- it THICKENS the crust to ~70 km, roughly double normal, and the range's sheer weight bows the plate down to form the flat Ganges plain. T5: Nanga Parbat at the western 'syntaxis' is being shoved up fastest of all, several mm a year.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himalayas; Britannica 'Himalayas'; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology_of_the_Himalayas; NPS 'Collisional Mountain Ranges'. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: the wonder is a slow, planet-scale COLLISION you can still watch happening. Invert every rung -- lead with the scene (a plateau you could see from space, seabed on a summit) and make the earth-process the answer. Accuracy rail: collision began ~50 Mya, crust ~70 km thick, India still moving a few cm/yr -- give ranges, not false precision. Dinner-test payoff = the marine-rock-on-the-summit rung and the doubled-crust rung. Distractors = other real ranges/plateaus (Andes, Altiplano) and real processes (subduction, rifting) so all four choices stay live -- don't let the stem name the collision the answer asks for. Lane border: the plate-tectonics THEORY is science-bank territory; here it must stay anchored to THIS place.

name: The Andes
scope: The spine of South America, the longest mountain range on any continent. Deep ladder. T1: the Andes run ~7,000 km down the whole western edge of South America through seven countries -- the LONGEST continental mountain range on Earth. T2: Aconcagua (6,961 m) in Argentina is the highest peak outside Asia -- the tallest mountain in the Americas and both the Southern and Western Hemispheres. T3: high in the central Andes spreads the Altiplano, a vast plain ~3,700 m up -- the world's second-highest plateau after Tibet. T3: the world's highest VOLCANOES rise here; Ojos del Salado (6,893 m) on the Chile-Argentina border is the highest volcano on Earth. T4: because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point on Earth's surface FARTHEST from the planet's center -- closer to space than Everest, though shorter. T5: why is there a range here at all? The oceanic Nazca plate dives BENEATH South America (subduction, not a continental collision), melting and feeding a chain of volcanoes -- teach: subduction zone. T5: on the Andes' western flank the descending cold current and rain shadow create the Atacama, the driest non-polar desert, where some weather stations have never recorded rain (one-rung mention; Atacama earns its own desert ladder).
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes; Guinness World Records 'Longest continental mountain range'; Britannica 'Andes Mountains'; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimborazo. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: superlative-as-hook, knowable-thing-as-answer. The Chimborazo 'farthest from Earth's center / closest to the stars' rung is the dinner-test payoff. Accuracy rail: length ~7,000 km, Aconcagua 6,961 m, Ojos del Salado 6,893 m -- and be precise that Aconcagua is highest OUTSIDE Asia (not on Earth). Distractors = other real ranges, real high peaks, real plateaus. Lane borders: the llama/vicuna/condor are the ANIMAL bank; Inca sites (Machu Picchu) are a separate ladder and possibly history -- this ladder stays on landscape and earth-process. Keep the Chimborazo rung's answer the PLACE, not the astronomy lecture.

name: Kilimanjaro
scope: Africa's highest mountain, rising alone from the East African savanna in Tanzania (Uhuru Peak 5,895 m). Deep ladder. T1: Kilimanjaro rises straight out of flat plains with no other mountains near it -- the tallest FREE-STANDING mountain in the world (not part of any range). T2: it is a volcano with THREE cones -- Kibo (the highest, holding Uhuru Peak), jagged Mawenzi, and old collapsed Shira, now a plateau. T3: though it sits almost on the EQUATOR, its summit wears glaciers and snow -- ice on the equator. T4: those summit glaciers are VANISHING -- shrunk by roughly 80%+ since 1912 and projected to disappear within decades. T4: Kibo isn't dead -- it's dormant, with a fresh inner crater ('Reusch Crater') and an ash pit that still smells of sulphur. T5: climb it and you pass through FIVE climate zones in a few days -- cultivated farmland, rainforest, heath and moorland, alpine desert, and an arctic summit -- like walking from the equator to the pole in one hike. T5: the mountain makes its OWN weather, pulling moist air up its flanks to feed the rainforest belt that rings its lower slopes.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kilimanjaro; kilimanjaropark.org / KINAPA; EBSCO Research Starters 'Mount Kilimanjaro'. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: a snow-capped peak floating over a hot savanna is the whole wonder -- lead with that image. The FIVE-climate-zones rung (equator-to-pole in one hike) is the dinner-test payoff; the equatorial-glaciers and free-standing rungs anchor the ladder. Accuracy rail: 'tallest free-standing mountain' and Uhuru 5,895 m are correct; frame the glacier loss as observed shrinkage + projection, not a fixed doomsday date. Distractors = other real African/volcanic features and other superlative mountains. Lane border: the elephants, giraffes, and colobus monkeys on the lower slopes are the ANIMAL bank -- the answer is always the place, its cones, its ice, its zones.

name: K2
scope: The world's second-highest mountain (8,611 m), in the Karakoram on the China-Pakistan border. Standard ladder. T1: K2 is the SECOND-highest mountain on Earth -- yet climbers fear it far more than Everest, and its nickname is the 'Savage Mountain.' T2: its odd name isn't a native word -- it's a SURVEY CODE; 19th-century British surveyors labelled the Karakoram peaks K1, K2, K3..., and because K2 is so remote it had no common local name, the code stuck. T3: there is no easy side -- every route is a steep, avalanche-raked pyramid of rock and ice, so historically about one climber has died for every four who reached the top. T4: for decades K2 defied WINTER -- it was the very last of the fourteen 8,000ers never climbed in the coldest season, in temperatures below -50 C and hurricane winds. T5: that final barrier fell on 16 January 2021, when an all-NEPALI team of ten summited together in winter and sang their national anthem on top -- the last great first of high-altitude mountaineering.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K2; National Geographic + PlanetMountain (2021 all-Nepali winter first ascent, team of 10, Jan 16 2021, -58 F); Britannica 'K2'. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: the hook is 'why fear the world's #2 more than #1?'. The 2021 all-Nepali winter first-ascent rung is the dinner-test payoff (place-anchored to the K2 summit). Accuracy rail: name = Karakoram survey code (K + number), NOT a local name; fatality figure is a historical ratio (~1 in 4) that has improved recently -- frame as 'historically.' Distractors = other real 8,000ers and their nicknames/facts (Annapurna's death rate, Nanga Parbat 'Killer Mountain'). Weight high: canonical peak.

name: The Karakoram
scope: A compact, savagely high range north of the Himalayas (China-Pakistan-India), home to K2. Standard ladder on the RANGE (K2 has its own ladder). T1: the Karakoram crams FOUR of the world's fourteen 8,000 m peaks -- K2, Broad Peak, and the two Gasherbrums -- into one small tangle of valleys, best seen from the Concordia junction ('the throne room of the mountain gods'). T2: its name means 'BLACK GRAVEL' in Turkic, for the dark rubble of its high passes. T3: outside the Arctic and Antarctic, the Karakoram is the most heavily GLACIATED place on Earth -- the Baltoro Glacier alone runs about 63 km. T4: while glaciers almost everywhere else are retreating, many Karakoram glaciers hold steady or even ADVANCE -- a real scientific puzzle named the 'Karakoram anomaly.' T5: the leading explanation is a rare local weather pattern (the 'Karakoram vortex') that keeps SUMMERS here cool and snowy while the rest of the Himalaya warms -- so the ice is fed, not starved.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karakoram + /Baltoro_Glacier; Princeton News 2014 + Nature Geoscience 2019 (Karakoram anomaly, Karakoram vortex); geographyworlds.com (Baltoro ~63 km). Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: a hidden range that out-does the Himalaya for sheer density of giants. The Karakoram-anomaly rung (glaciers GROWING while the world's retreat) is the dinner-test payoff; frame the vortex as the LEADING explanation, still studied, not settled fact. Accuracy rail: four 8,000ers here (K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum I & II), Baltoro ~63 km, 'most glaciated outside the poles.' Distractors = other real ranges/glaciers and other 8,000ers. Keep separate from the K2 ladder -- these are the RANGE's wonders (glaciers, concentration, anomaly), not the single peak's.

name: The Matterhorn
scope: The iconic pyramid peak on the Swiss-Italian border (4,478 m). Standard ladder. T1: the Matterhorn's fame is its SHAPE -- a lonely, near-perfect pyramid with four steep faces, each pointing to a compass direction (the Toblerone silhouette). T2: that horn was CARVED by ice -- glaciers gnawing at four sides at once ground the peak into a pyramid; a peak shaped this way is literally called a 'horn' (teach: glacial horn, from four cirques). T3: the rock at the very SUMMIT came from AFRICA -- it is a slice of the African tectonic plate (the Dent Blanche nappe) shoved up and over Europe, so the top of a Swiss mountain is African bedrock. T4: its first ascent, in 1865, ended in TRAGEDY -- four of the seven climbers fell to their deaths on the descent when the rope between them snapped. T5: the peak is slowly coming APART -- the permafrost 'glue' inside it is thawing, loosening rock and triggering rockfalls that reshape the famous ridges.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matterhorn (Dent Blanche nappe African-plate gneiss; 1865 Whymper ascent, 4 of 7 died on descent; four glacier-carved faces); earthlymission.com (African summit). Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: the shape everyone can draw hides three deeper wonders. The 'African rock on top of a Swiss mountain' rung is the dinner-test payoff. Accuracy rail: summit gneiss is African-plate rock (Dent Blanche nappe); first ascent 1865, rope broke on descent killing four; a glacially-carved pyramid is technically a 'horn.' Distractors = other real Alpine peaks (Eiger, Weisshorn, Mont Blanc) and real landforms (arete, cirque, aiguille). Lane border: keep the T5 permafrost/rockfall rung about the ROCK, not climate-policy commentary.

name: Mount Fuji
scope: Japan's sacred, near-symmetrical volcano (3,776 m). Standard ladder that mixes earth-process and cultural-creation-born-here rungs. T1: Fuji is Japan's tallest mountain and a near-perfect, symmetrical CONE -- the shape the whole world pictures for a volcano (a stratovolcano). T2: it IS an active volcano; it last erupted in 1707, blanketing Edo (old Tokyo) ~100 km away in ash for weeks (the Hoei eruption). T3: the smooth cone hides a secret -- Fuji is really THREE volcanoes stacked over time, the modern peak grown atop two older, buried volcanoes. T4: its beauty made it a CULTURAL creation -- Hokusai's woodblock series 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji' (with the Great Wave) carried the cone around the world; UNESCO lists Fuji for its CULTURE, not its nature. T4: it is a holy mountain, climbed by pilgrims for centuries, its summit ringed by shrines. T5: Fuji sits where THREE tectonic plates meet under Japan (a rare triple junction of the Eurasian, Pacific, and Philippine Sea plates) -- which is exactly why a volcano stands here.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoei_eruption; Smithsonian Magazine + NatGeo Education (last eruption Dec 1707); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Fuji (stratovolcano, three volcanoes, UNESCO cultural site, triple junction); Hokusai 'Thirty-Six Views'. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: a place whose wonders are BOTH earth-science and human-made-here. The UNESCO-listed-for-CULTURE-not-nature rung is the dinner-test twist; the triple-junction rung is the earth-science payoff. Accuracy rail: last confirmed eruption 1707 Hoei event (label it dormant/active, not extinct); the Hokusai series is a real cultural creation genuinely born of this place (a legitimate geography rung, not a food/art detour). Distractors = other real volcanoes and Japanese landmarks. Keep the Hokusai rung's answer the ARTWORK-of-this-place, and don't drift into art-history technique.

name: Mount Kailash
scope: A remote, unclimbed sacred peak in western Tibet (6,638 m). Standard ladder. T1: Kailash is a striking, near-symmetrical black-and-snow peak that -- unlike almost every other major Himalayan summit -- has NEVER been climbed. T2: it is unclimbed on PURPOSE: four different religions hold it sacred (Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and the older Bon faith), and all consider standing on its summit a sacrilege, so climbing is banned. T3: four of Asia's GREAT RIVERS rise near its four faces -- the Indus, the Sutlej, the Brahmaputra, and the Karnali (a Ganges headwater). T4: pilgrims do not climb it -- they WALK AROUND it, a ~52 km circuit called the kora, some measuring the whole loop in full body-length prostrations, and Bon pilgrims circle the opposite way from the rest. T5: to Hindus and Buddhists the mountain is the earthly form of Mount Meru, the mythic axis at the CENTER of the universe -- label this as sacred cosmology/belief, not settled fact.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kailash; Britannica 'Mount Kailash' (sacred to Hinduism/Buddhism/Jainism/Bon; four rivers; kora ~52 km); unclimbed status. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: the wonder is a mountain whose greatest 'feature' is that no one has ever stood on top -- and why. The four-great-rivers rung is the dinner-test payoff. Accuracy rail: name the four faiths and treat them EQUALLY and neutrally (no favoring); label the Mount Meru rung explicitly as religious cosmology; 'unclimbed' means no recorded successful ascent + it is now prohibited. Distractors = other real sacred peaks (Fuji, Adam's Peak, Uluru) and other river sources. Even though four religions appear, the treatment is descriptive and symmetric -- no stance is required.

name: The Alps
scope: Europe's great mountain arc (~1,200 km, eight countries), highest peak Mont Blanc (4,808 m). Deep ladder. T1: the Alps curve across the heart of Europe; their highest point, the 'White Mountain' Mont Blanc, is the roof of Western Europe. T2: Mont Blanc's first climb, in 1786, effectively BIRTHED the sport of mountaineering -- a doctor and a crystal-hunter reached the top for a long-standing cash prize. T3: the Alps were BORN when Africa crashed into Europe, crushing an ancient ocean (the Tethys) shut -- which is why marine fossils and old seafloor rock now sit on Alpine peaks. T4: the collision shoved rock layers so hard they FOLDED OVER themselves and slid tens of km, forming giant overturned sheets geologists call 'nappes' (teach the term). T4: the Alps are the water tower of Europe -- the Rhine, Rhone, Po, and tributaries of the Danube all rise here. T5: the Alps are where science DISCOVERED the Ice Ages -- 19th-century naturalists here realized vanished glaciers once buried Europe. T5: in 1991 a 5,300-year-old frozen body, 'Otzi the Iceman,' melted out of an Alpine glacier, perfectly preserved with his copper axe -- the place kept a Stone Age man on ice for millennia.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alps + /Geology_of_the_Alps; tethyswater.ch (Africa-Europe collision, Tethys closure, ~1-3 cm/yr); 1786.travel + Wikipedia 'Jacques Balmat' (1786 first ascent Balmat & Paccard); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otzi. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: a range that gave the world both a sport and a science. The Otzi-the-Iceman rung is the dinner-test payoff (place kept a 5,300-yr-old man frozen); the Africa-Europe collision / seafloor-on-the-peaks rung is the earth-science anchor. Accuracy rail: Mont Blanc 4,808 m, first ascent 1786 (Balmat & Paccard), Alps from Africa-Europe collision closing the Tethys. Distractors = other real ranges and Alpine peaks. Lane note: Mont Blanc's 1786 climb is mountaineering history (keep the answer the place/first-ascent-birthed-alpinism, not a bare bio); the Matterhorn has its OWN ladder -- reference but don't duplicate.
history_overlap: Otzi the Iceman (and possibly the discovery of the Ice Ages) could appear as a history/archaeology episode; here both are framed as wonders the ALPINE PLACE produced -- keep the answer the place-fact, not a standalone history vignette.

name: The Appalachians
scope: The ancient, worn range of eastern North America -- low, rounded, forested. Standard ladder built on deep time. T1: the Appalachians roll as gentle, rounded, tree-covered ridges -- the worn-down NUBS of what were once towering peaks (old mountains are low and smooth; young ones jagged). T2: they are OLD beyond imagining -- they rose about 480 million years ago, before trees existed and around the dawn of the first animals with backbones ('older than bones'). T3: they are even OLDER than SATURN'S RINGS, which recent studies date to only ~100-200 million years -- a mountain range on Earth predates a feature of another planet. T4: when they first formed they were HIMALAYAN in scale -- the continental collision that raised them helped assemble the supercontinent Pangaea. T5: the same range is SPLIT across the ocean -- its torn-off other halves are the Scottish Highlands and Morocco's Atlas Mountains, separated when the Atlantic Ocean opened and drifted them apart.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_Mountains (Ordovician ~480 Mya orogenies; Central Pangean Mountains; Caledonian/Atlas correlation); studycountry.com + onceinabluemoon.ca (Appalachians vs Saturn's rings ~100-200 Mya); AVLtoday. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: the whole ladder is a deep-time gut-punch -- these gentle hills are impossibly ancient. The 'older than Saturn's rings' rung is the dinner-test payoff; the 'torn halves are in Scotland and Morocco' rung is the second twist. Accuracy rail: orogeny ~480-300 Mya (core rocks ~1.2 Gyr -- distinguish rock age from range age); Saturn's-ring youth is a RECENT finding, label it as such; 'older than bones' = predates land vertebrates, frame it that way not literally. Distractors = other real old/young ranges (Urals, Rockies, Himalaya) and real correlated ranges. No lane conflicts.

name: Denali
scope: North America's highest peak, in Alaska (6,190 m / 20,310 ft). Standard ladder. T1: Denali is the highest mountain in North America; its Koyukon (Alaska Native) name means 'the High One' / 'the Tall One.' T2: by one measure it out-does even Everest -- Denali rises higher from its BASE to its summit than any other mountain on land (~5,500 m of vertical relief, versus roughly 3,600-4,000 m for Everest above its plateau). T3: it is one of the COLDEST mountains on Earth -- its far-north latitude plus great height make the summit brutally cold, colder than the elevation alone would explain. T4: because it sits so far north, the atmosphere is 'squashed' lower at the poles, so the air at Denali's summit is THINNER than at the same height near the equator -- climbers feel as if they are even higher than 6,190 m. T5: Denali is still RISING -- it sits beside the Denali Fault, where the Pacific plate grinds under Alaska and keeps lifting the whole Alaska Range.
source: WebSearch-corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denali + /Denali-Mount_McKinley_naming_dispute; USGS 20,310 ft (2015); Britannica 'Denali' (greatest relief on land, ~17,000 ft above plain); coverage of the Jan 2025 federal reversion to Mount McKinley. Build stage should corroborate on Grokipedia first.
framing_note: Voice: the hook is 'how does a shorter mountain beat Everest?' -- the base-to-peak / greatest-vertical-relief-on-land rung is the dinner-test payoff. Accuracy rail on the NAME (handle neutrally, as fact): the Koyukon name is Denali ('the High One'); the U.S. federal name was McKinley 1917-2015, Denali 2015-2025, and was reverted to Mount McKinley by executive order in Jan 2025 -- state this plainly, no editorializing, and keep every rung's ANSWER a geographic fact (relief, cold, thin air, uplift), never the name-politics itself. Distractors = other real high/cold/high-relief peaks (Everest, Aconcagua, Mount Logan, Mount Rainier). No lane conflicts.
